question.problem: The graph of the function $y=f(x)$ passes through $(-4,2)$ and is concave up on the interval $(-6,-3).$ If ${f}^{′}(-4)=-2,$ estimate the value of $f(-3.8)$ using the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $x=-4$ and determine whether the approximation is an underestimate or overestimate.
question.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $a=-4$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(-4)+{f}^{′}(-4)(x+4).\end{aligned}
$$

The function passes through the point $(-4,2),$ so we have $f(-4)=2.$ Also, we're told that ${f}^{′}(-4)=-2,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =2+(-2)(x+4) \\  & =2-2(x+4).\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $f(-3.8)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=-3.8.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-3.8) & ≈L(-3.8) \\  & =2-2(-3.8+4) \\  & =2-2(0.2) \\  & =1.6.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the function is concave up on the interval $(-6,-3),$ the linear approximation $L(x)$ is below the graph near $x=-4,$ and therefore we have an underestimate.
